decision: ADR-0070 (the full meal structure); operations/sprint2-plan/08-household.md section 0
note: Read by the planner (app/data/meal_structure.py), not the importer. Every value below is a design value MealCraft chose, tunable on developer data only; none is an HPB or protocol figure.

presets.note: The full default per meal (ADR-0070 section 1). A role with min_people is planned only when at least that many people eat the meal; a role with required false is the one dish the planner may leave out when the budget, time, energy floor or dishes cannot fit it.

portion_shares.note: Servings of each dish per person at the meal. protein_main and vegetable list the share for 1, 2, 3 ... such dishes; a one-bowl core (or any meal of one dish) is a whole serving.

energy_floor_share.note: A lunch or dinner gives every member at it at least this share of that member's daily energy target (ADR-0070 section 3). Member targets are the HPB energy times the goal factor, and a member's servings are that target over the adult reference, so the floor per serving is the share times the adult reference energy.

soft.note: Meal-level terms added to a meal's rank loss (ADR-0075 order: variety, nutrition, rank, price). Small next to a dish's rank loss (0 to 1.5).

staple_defaults.note: Plain staples (release recipe ids): the grain or dough with water, salt, oil or butter only, chosen by a title and ingredient rule over the staple-tagged release recipes and reviewed by hand on 2026-10-19. 'Rice by default' means these come first; any other staple-tagged recipe (a dish of its own, such as a cheese pasta) costs not_plain. The release has no plain Chinese steamed rice; a curated staple file would add one (a data-layer change).

staple_kind_by_group.note: The plain staple kinds a meal of each cuisine group usually has (data/recipes/cuisine-groups.json); 'none' is a meal whose core dish has no group.
